successors.name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1607 (May): the Virginia Company founds Jamestown, the first English colony.
1608: East India Company traders settle at Surat.
1609: Bermuda is settled by accident after the Sea Venture wreck.
1610: Cuper's Cove is founded in Newfoundland.
1615: Renews is founded in Newfoundland (page: founded, abandoned 1619).
1617: the London and Bristol Company founds Cambriol in Newfoundland (page: abandoned by 1637).
1620: the Pilgrims found Plymouth Colony.
1621 (August): the first settlers reach Ferryland, Newfoundland.
1622: the Province of Maine is granted.
1623: New Hampshire is settled (overseas possessions page).
1623: the English settle Saint Kitts.
1625: England settles Barbados, a major English settlement (page: first visited by the Olive Blossom in 1605).
1628: Nevis is settled (overseas possessions page: Nevis settled 1628).
1629: Puritans found the Massachusetts Bay Colony.
1629: four cells appear in Sierra Leone (7.5N 12.7W) and stay to 1669.
1629: the English also seize Acadia and Cape Breton Island.
1629 (19 July): David Kirke's English fleet takes Quebec.
1632: Antigua is settled by colonists from Saint Kitts (overseas possessions page).
1632: Montserrat is settled (overseas possessions page).
1632 (29 March): England gives Quebec, Acadia and Cape Breton back at Saint-Germain-en-Laye.
1634: Maryland is founded.
1636: Connecticut is established (page: established 1636, chartered as a royal colony in 1662).
1636: Roger Williams founds Providence Plantations (page: Roger Williams established Providence Plantations in 1636).
1638: New Haven is founded (overseas possessions page: founded 1638, merged with Connecticut 1665; the Thirteen Colonies page says 1664).
1639: the East India Company buys Madrasapatnam and builds Fort St.
1640: two cells appear on the Gold Coast.
1648: Bermudians, the Eleutheran Adventurers, settle Eleuthera in the Bahamas (page: Eleuthera left to the Eleutheran Adventurers from Bermuda to settle).
1648: Virginia grows from 9 to 46 cells.
1650: Lord Willoughby's colony is founded on the Suriname River.
1653: six North Carolina cells appear.
1655: England conquers Jamaica from Spain under Cromwell.
1661: Tangier comes to England with Catherine of Braganza's dowry.
1661: Bombay is transferred to England in Catherine of Braganza's dowry (page: Bombay transferred to England as part of Catherine's dowry, prior holder Portugal).
1664: Delaware and the former New Sweden land are taken from the Dutch.
1664 (27 August): the English fleet takes New Amsterdam.
1664 (September): New Netherland is English; the page describes the Duke of York's province as running from Long Island, up the Hudson and Mohawk valleys, to the Great Lakes.
1664 (29 September): the surrender of New Netherland ends the fighting (infobox: surrender of New Netherland, 29 September 1664).
1665-1666: Mahim, Sion, Dharavi and Wadala are acquired from the Portuguese on Bombay (page: 1665-1666, acquired from the Portuguese).
1667: Suriname goes to the Dutch.
1670: the Sierra Leone cells vanish from the shape.
1670: Charles II grants the Hudson's Bay Company its charter.
1670: Carolina is settled at Charles Town.
1670 (8 July): Spain accepts English logwood stations on the coast.
1673: the shape draws 44 Bahamas cells.
1673: Fort James, Ghana, is listed as an English possession (overseas possessions page).
1673 (July): a Dutch fleet retakes New York.

1674 (5 March): the Treaty of Westminster returns New York to England (infobox: Treaty of Westminster, 5 March 1674); the Duke of York gets a second grant in July 1674 and appoints Edmund Andros governor.
1681: William Penn's Pennsylvania is founded (page: founded in 1681 as a proprietary colony).
1684: England abandons Tangier (page: abandoned 1684).
1687: the four Surat cells vanish from the shape.
1687: Virginia grows from 53 to 84 cells.
1687: a Hudson Bay post at about 57N 92.5W enters the shape.
1690: the East India Company settles Calcutta (page: Calcutta, Bengal, settled by the East India Company in 1690).
1696: the Hudson Bay post at 57N leaves the shape.
1702: Carolina grows from 10 to 22 cells and Virginia by three; a James Bay post at 52.3N 82W appears.
1707: the English colonies become British.
1713: the colonies pass to the British Colonial Empire row.
1762: Bombay is carried by the British Empire row (which draws Madras, Bombay and Masulipatnam in 1762); this row has no 1762 shape.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1763: the Chingleput jaghire becomes the Madras presidency's first district (page: it was obtained in 1763).
1763: two cells at Masulipatnam enter the shape.
1778: Masulipatnam leaves this row's shape; the British Empire row has drawn it since 1769.

ledger.x: 1779: the last shape of the row ends; the British Empire row draws Madras from 1780.

wars.name: Anglo-French War (1627-1629)
wars.outcome: An English fleet under David Kirke took Quebec on 19 July 1629 and the English seized Acadia and Cape Breton; the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye of 29 March 1632 returned all of New France to France.

wars.name: Anglo-Spanish War (1654-1660)
wars.outcome: England joined France against Spain in late 1654, failed at Hispaniola and took Jamaica; in the Caribbean the war went on as privateer raids until the Treaty of Madrid of 8 July 1670, which adopted only the principle of actual possession.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Dutch War
wars.outcome: England took New Netherland (27 August to 29 September 1664); the Dutch took Suriname in 1667 and the English retook it five months later; the Treaty of Breda was signed in July 1667, and the exchange of Suriname for New York was only de facto, 'under the…

wars.name: Third Anglo-Dutch War
wars.outcome: A Dutch fleet recaptured New York in July 1673; the Treaty of Westminster of 5 March 1674 returned it to England.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Utrecht (main treaties of 11 April 1713) gave Britain Nova Scotia, claims to Newfoundland, 'territories in Rupert's Land' and the French part of Saint Kitts, and Gibraltar and Menorca from Spain (13 July 1713).

certainty.note: Colonial frontiers are charter claims and settled enclaves, not surveyed lines: the Treaty of Madrid page says the treaty of 8 July 1670 set no boundaries and adopted only the principle of actual possession.
Madras, Bombay and Masulipatnam are small company enclaves round forts; their limits follow grants (the Chingleput jaghire of 1763) and were not surveyed.
